name: List the outcomes of a chance experiment
description: Student can list all the possible outcomes of a chance experiment.
exampleOfSuccess: For rolling a dice, the student lists 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.
commonError: Student misses an outcome or lists impossible ones.
checkpointTask: Name chance experiments. Ask the student to list the possible outcomes.

name: Identify equally likely outcomes
description: Student can identify when outcomes are equally likely.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says heads and tails on a fair coin are equally likely.
commonError: Student calls outcomes equally likely when they are not.
checkpointTask: Pose experiments. Ask the student whether the outcomes are equally likely.

name: Compare equally and not equally likely outcomes
description: Student can compare experiments with equally likely outcomes to those without.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a fair spinner is equally likely, but an uneven one is not.
commonError: Student treats all experiments as equally likely.
checkpointTask: Show fair and unfair experiments. Ask the student to compare the likelihoods.

name: Reason about the chance of winning
description: Student can reason about the chance of an outcome by considering the number of ways it can happen.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says a colour with more sections on a spinner is more likely.
commonError: Student judges by preference rather than the number of favourable outcomes.
checkpointTask: Pose a game of chance. Ask the student to reason about the chance of winning.

name: Conduct a repeated chance experiment
description: Student can conduct a repeated chance experiment and record the results.
exampleOfSuccess: The student spins a spinner many times and tallies the results.
commonError: Student runs too few trials or does not record each result.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to run repeated trials and record the results.

name: Use frequency to compare outcomes
description: Student can use the frequency of results to compare outcomes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student compares how often each colour came up across the trials.
commonError: Student compares single trials rather than the totals.
checkpointTask: After trials, ask the student to compare the outcomes using the frequencies.

name: Estimate likelihood from results
description: Student can use experimental results to estimate the likelihood of an outcome.
exampleOfSuccess: From the tallies, the student estimates red is about half the spins.
commonError: Student ignores the results when estimating likelihood.
checkpointTask: After trials, ask the student to estimate the likelihood of each outcome.

name: Compare results with and without equally likely outcomes
description: Student can compare results from experiments with and without equally likely outcomes.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notes the fair coin evened out but the weighted spinner favoured one colour.
commonError: Student expects all experiments to even out the same way.
checkpointTask: Run a fair and an unfair experiment. Ask the student to compare the results.
